<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert (route, the route ledger binds it to client method packages.revertCommit))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via listPackageBindings (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via revertCommit (symbol, a method of class ProtocolPackageCommitsFacet))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee11fce924ee0be609807738a3e0770cf6c396a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ad2cc02da96ea9fe63c8c2a4f8705f605e0f3d81` — the merge of head `43a6758fe8859a4e4b6a96a7ea49cceaae6fae63` into base `ee11fce924ee0be609807738a3e0770cf6c396a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ad2cc02da96ea9fe63c8c2a4f8705f605e0f3d81 && git checkout ad2cc02da96ea9fe63c8c2a4f8705f605e0f3d81
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ee11fce924ee0be609807738a3e0770cf6c396a3 43a6758fe8859a4e4b6a96a7ea49cceaae6fae63 && git checkout -B drift-repro ee11fce924ee0be609807738a3e0770cf6c396a3 && git merge --no-ff 43a6758fe8859a4e4b6a96a7ea49cceaae6fae63

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee11fce924ee0be609807738a3e0770cf6c396a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ee11fce924ee0be609807738a3e0770cf6c396a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `43a6758fe8859a4e4b6a96a7ea49cceaae6fae63`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-slots.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/metadata/src/index.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-history-slots.33308.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-slots.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.platform-mark-rollback.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/history-diff-two-holders-33308.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/37130-platform-record-restore-doors.md, .changeset/37013-platform-skill-own-slot.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-class-head.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/batch-object-registration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commit-record.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-commit.object.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and on `.changeset/37130-platform-record-restore-doors.md`; no published schema and no governed path in the 14-file list, none under `.claude/**`). Inputs: card #37130 with its six comments, PR #37423 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at merge base `ecbe854b`), and the check-runs on the head. The review began on `abc706ce`; the head then moved to `43a6758f`. I read `git diff abc706ce..43a6758f` myself: two files, both under `.changeset/`, 6 insertions and 2 deletions, so every code and test hunk judged below is byte-identical on this head. The seat's note that moved the head also named the changeset correction as a duty; its two claims (a changeset-only delta, and a `Check Changeset` red that is the deliberate-correction class) were checked against the tree and the job log, not adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `rollbackMetaItem` refuses a restore whose active row is the platform's own record: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, nothing written (`protocol-package-commits.ts:2268`, judged at `sys-metadata-repository.ts:2026` on the row the same call then writes). Right: card item 1, the service door's own refusal function.
2. The restore limb of `revertCommit` refuses the same row per item, into `failed[]` with `code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, and the commit's other items still revert (`protocol-package-commits.ts:1732`; the per-item `catch` pushes to `failed[]`, and `revertPlan.push` sits after `restoreVersion`, so a refused item is not in the revert's own commit). Right: ADR-0067 D3 as amended runs per item.
3. The history, diff and rollback `?package=` selector refuses a package that neither holds a row of the name nor ships it, also when the package-less row is stored (`protocol-history-slots.ts:206-210`). Right, and it is the spec's own refusal made real: `HISTORY_PACKAGE_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:2727`, unchanged on `main`) already says "a package that neither holds nor ships the name is refused 409 `not-held-by-qualifier`". What is taken away is a behaviour that description contradicted; the description needs no edit, since a shipper still addresses the package-less row.
4. Public surface added: `refusePlatformRecordRestore` exported from `@objectstack/metadata` (`packages/metadata/src/index.ts`), and the optional `refusePlatformRecord` option of `SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` (the class is exported at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts:246`). Right: additive, default off, no caller changes behaviour without passing it. The private `refusePlatformRecordRollback` it replaces was never exported, so nothing is removed.
5. The refusal's message gains one clause; code and status are unchanged. Right as to the envelope; the clause is N1.
6. `MetadataManager.list()` after the boot priming pass lists a row whose body stamp differs from its column once, under the column (`primedRowSlot`, `metadata-manager.ts:1911`); a read naming the stamp's package no longer answers the primed copy. Right: it is what an unprimed process over the same rows answers, and the new pin holds a cold-manager control.
7. `listPackageBindings` answers `degraded: true`, naming the loader, over a `datasource:` loader with no `loadRowBindings`. Right: `packages/spec/src/contracts/metadata-service.ts:463` already tells a gating consumer to treat a degraded answer as unknown, so no contract text moves. `DatabaseLoader` is the only `datasource:` loader in the tree and offers the method.
8. `bindReadRowPackage` records the column the re-read finds; the node that lost the first-boot race answers the bound package, not `null`. Right, and no query is added: the re-read predates the hunk.
9. No schema key, accepted value, error code, refusal reason or route is added: `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and `not-held-by-qualifier` both exist. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
10. Three expectations are inverted to the 409 the ruling states (one unit case, its 33308 twin, one dogfood case). Right: each pinned the branch card item 2 removes.

Gate verdicts, read as check-run conclusions on `43a6758f` at record time: every run has concluded (read 2026-11-26T04:20Z, head unchanged). Success: `Build Core`, `Test Core` and all ten of its shards, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`, `Lint & Repo Gates` with its eight `Lint ·` jobs, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. Failure: `Check Changeset`, both runs, for the single reason judged in ② (the deliberate correction of a pending note); its level, ADR-0087 and major-bump lines pass. Eighteen runs are skipped (UI build and opt-in families this diff does not select). The dev's two local NOT MEASURED families are answered by these runs.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37130-platform-record-restore-doors.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a BREAKING banner with a "What to do" line under each breaking bullet, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). Right. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 sets the level by the metadata-protocol kind alone, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition; nothing an author can write is added, refused or re-meant here. The `Check Changeset` job prints the same reading on this head: "LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `yes (narrowing)` and metadata-protocol `none` ... a non-protocol change at `patch`", and "1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition". `yes` in place of the claim's `no` is right: the diff adds public surface (① item 4).

The new section "Also in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`" of that note reads: "`SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` takes `refusePlatformRecord: true` to ask `refusePlatformRecordRestore` (`@objectstack/metadata`) on the row it writes; the undo writes do not pass it." Right, sentence by sentence: the option is declared at `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1952`; it is asked on `activeRow`, the row `put` then updates; and neither undo write passes it (`batch-object-registration.ts:351`, `protocol-history-and-publish.ts:162`). Moving it out of the `@objectstack/metadata` list is right, since the class ships from the other package. The bullet left under `@objectstack/metadata` ("`refusePlatformRecordRestore(type, name, row)` is exported: the one refusal the service's `rollback` and the protocol's two restore doors ask") is right: `database-loader.ts:1932` and `sys-metadata-repository.ts:2026` call the one function.

**Deliberate correction of a pending note: `.changeset/37013-platform-skill-own-slot.md`.** `Check Changeset` is red on this head in both of its runs for exactly one reason, the `check-empty-changeset` refusal that this file "exists on the merge base and was not added by this PR"; every other line of the job is a pass. The PR body declares the correction under "Deliberate correction" and names the note. `git diff abc706ce..43a6758f` shows one line of that file changed, in three places, with the frontmatter and the rest of the bullet untouched. Per `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md`, this record judges each rewritten sentence against the tree, before and after:

- Strip sentence. Before: "... and so do the metadata protocol's save door and its restore doors (`rollbackMetaItem` and the restore limb of `revertCommit`); a stored row the boot pass re-registers keeps it only when the row held it as read." After: "... and so do the metadata protocol's save door and its restore doors (`rollbackMetaItem` and the restore limb of `revertCommit`) on every restore whose row is not the platform's own record; a stored row ...". On `main` the Before was true of every restore (the door pins were red there because the platform's row was written back). On this head a restore over the platform's row writes nothing, so the Before over-states and the After is exact: the strip is `withoutPlatformOrigin` in `restoredBodyWriter` (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts:135`), which both doors receive through `restoreWriteFor`, and the refusal precedes the write. Right.
- Refusal sentence. Before: "`rollback` whose row is the platform's own record is refused (`409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, naming the fix), with nothing written." After: "A restore whose row is the platform's own record is refused (`409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, naming the fix), with nothing written, at all three restore doors: `rollback`, and the metadata protocol's `rollbackMetaItem` and the restore limb of `revertCommit`." The Before named one door of three on this head. The After matches `database-loader.ts:1932`, `protocol-package-commits.ts:2268` and `:1732`. At `revertCommit` the refusal is per item, in `failed[]`, which the 37130 note states beside it. Right.
- `getPublished` sentence. Before: "`getPublished` serves it on the answer's top level only when the stored item carries it there, and never inside a publish snapshot;" After: "`getPublished` serves it on the answer's top level only when the stored item carries it there (the platform's own record's publish snapshot, served as the answer, keeps the mark it carries at its top), and never on a snapshot nested inside the answer;". The code is the same on `main` and on this head (`metadata-manager.ts:3612`, `withoutServedPlatformMarks` at `:742`): the answer is the item's `publishedDefinition` when it has one, `keepTop` is `carriesPlatformStamp(item)`, and only a `publishedDefinition` nested in the answer is always stripped. So the Before was already inexact when it merged (a snapshot served as the answer can keep the mark), and the After is exact. Right. One note on the PR body's framing: this PR did not make that third sentence false, it was imprecise before; that is a wording matter of the PR body only and is folded into N4.
- "of a failed batch row write", left unchanged on purpose: no longer the exact wording, and it was not exact before either. `undoBatchRowWrite` undoes a row whose write landed and whose registration the registry then refused (`settleBatchObjectRows`, `batch-object-registration.ts`; both callers' messages say "the registry refuses it"). A write that failed leaves nothing to undo. The same diff corrects this phrase in the code (`PLATFORM_PROVENANCE`: "the undo of a batch row the registry refused (`undoBatchRowWrite`)"), so the code doc and the pending note now differ. Graded N3.

The correction is confirmed for the three rewritten sentences.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open question (the export and the option without a maintainer decision): on the design, option A is right and I find no fork. (a) It is an additive export of a refusal the producer already shipped privately (`refusePlatformRecordRollback`), from the entry that since #37013 exports the mark's one definition to the same consumer (`PLATFORM_PROVENANCE`, `carriesPlatformStamp`, `isPlatformOrigin`, `withoutPlatformOrigin`, beside `historyRowAttribution`). (b) The card rules "the same prescription as the service's `rollback`"; option B is a second copy of code, status and sentence in `metadata-protocol`, which is the drift the card closes. (c) The option is optional and off by default, and the two undo writes stay byte for byte. (d) No error code, reason value, schema key or route is added.

On the route, two texts govern and I read them together. `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` (the stop section) has a change to a published export reported as `needs_decision`; pm-dispatch SKILL.md's escalation frame lands a new export name that has a producer precedent under the veto window, with the seat naming the precedent. A new export is not a change to a published one, so the second text governs the export, and its precedent is (a). The optional option on the already-published `restoreVersion` is nearer the first text's letter, though it is additive and changes no existing call. The dev reported `done` and asked, where the stricter reading would have stopped first: a process note for the seat, not rework. Answer: acceptable without a decision card, provided the seat's ACCEPT names both additions and the precedent so the maintainer's veto window covers them. This record does not rule in the maintainer's place; if the seat reads the option under the first text, it goes to him, and nothing in this review depends on which.

Deviations:
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` where the claim read `no (narrowing)`: right, see ②.
- The dogfood file outside the claim's surface, and its unit twin, retargeted to the 409: accepted. Both pinned the removed branch and would be red otherwise; the edit is the minimum, and the surviving branch (a shipper addressing the package-less row) keeps its unit pin through `shippers: [BETA]`.
- PR body stale on three readings at `abc706ce`: the body on this head carries the re-run figures. One line is stale again, N4.
- Two local gate families NOT MEASURED: CI answers them; see the gate verdicts in ①.

Carriers the report names, each answered:
- The ADR-0010 note wording, to the weekly ADR revisions card: accepted; the claim put `docs/adr/**` out of surface and the PR body gives the line.
- The pending 37013 note: closed on this head by the correction above, except N3.
- Round 4's other R21 reading (after the platform withdraws its record under a one-holder name, a rollback naming the package can write a version the platform registered into the package's row): not in card item 1, whose target is the platform's row, and not changed here. Escalated to the seat: it has no card, and a carrier with no card is lost at merge.
- #37187's N3 and N6: untouched, as stated; they stay with #37187's ACCEPT.

SQL push-down: no finding. No hunk adds a query, an id materialisation or an in-app join. `restoreVersion` judges the `activeRow` it already read, `bindReadRowPackage` reuses its existing re-read, `historySlotOf` asks the same two reads as before, and `primedRowSlot` and the `listPackageBindings` branch are in memory.

Security line: `no`. No hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The refusals apply to every caller alike and address which row a door writes or reads; `degraded` is a completeness signal.

Read outside the diff, not reviewed, for the seat: `adoptOrphans` (`protocol-package-commits.ts`, the orphan filter near line 897) rebinds every package-less row that is not artifact-backed by its column alone, and I found no exclusion of the platform's own record there. Read, not measured. If it holds, an adopted platform row keeps the mark under a package's column, and N5 applies to it.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it makes the spec's own refusal real (① item 3) and takes no declared capability away. The restore refusal is new behaviour the card rules, at doors whose spec text names no platform record.

Per file, against the card and the cited code:

- `sys-metadata-repository.ts`: holds. The check sits after the read of the row the write addresses and before `put`, so "judged on the row it writes, before anything is written" is true sentence by sentence. Earlier refusals of the same call (`VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, the tombstone, a refused body) can answer first; each also writes nothing.
- `protocol-package-commits.ts`: holds. Both doors always state `packageId`, so the row judged is the row restored. Tried: bare rollback of a platform-only name (refused); `?package=` of a shipper falling back to the platform's row (slot `null`, refused here or at the package-less close before it); `?package=` of a non-shipper (refused earlier by item 2); the two undo writes (unchanged, they are the only other `restoreVersion` callers); `rollbackToPackageCommit` (goes through `revertCommit`).
- `protocol-history-slots.ts`: holds. The only branch that changes is `slot === null` with a package that does not ship the name. A package's own row, its `.custom` pair's declared override, the unserved-row branch, and the row-held-base recursion (the base holds a row when the bare door asks) all answer as before.
- `database-loader.ts`: holds. `registerRollback` asks the same predicate on the same row as before; the function is the old one with the row test moved inside. The `storedRowBodyOf` comment sits on its function. N7's record is taken only for a legacy row the read handed out.
- `metadata-manager.ts`: holds. `primedRowSlot` answers only for a body a row loader handed out (`readRowColumnOf`), on the boot pass (`skipSourceLoader`, whose one caller is `plugin.ts:1821`), with a filled column and a different stamp; every other write keeps the write rule's key. The unstamped-body sentence agrees with `withEntryPackage`, which stamps a body that names no package with its entry's.
- `package-slotted-store.ts`: holds. Each sentence of the reworded `PLATFORM_PROVENANCE` doc matches the code: the strip list, the three refusing doors, the two undo writes by what they undo, and the snapshot rule.
- `index.ts`: holds.
- The five test files: the pins assert the refusal, the unchanged row and the surviving item; the selector pins assert reason, caller and candidates; the `list()`, N2 and N7 pins carry a control or an exact write count. Their red-on-base and ablation counts are the dev's reading, not re-run here.

Nits (none changes correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — the prescription's new clause, "to make an earlier version the environment's own item of the name, save that version's body again" (`database-loader.ts`, repeated in the 37130 note), names a route whose result lasts until the platform's next registration: the pending 37013 note states that a package-less environment write under a platform name "takes the bare slot without the stamp, and the platform's next registration restores its record". The same message says the platform registers again at its next boot, so a reader can infer it, but the clause does not say it.
- N2 (nit) — the `revertCommit` door pin and the RESTART pin serve a commit row with no `package_id`. `recordPackageCommit` (`protocol-package-commit-record.ts:56`, `packageId: string`) is the only writer of that table, and the limb's own comment says it never writes the package-less row. With a commit that names its package the limb reads that package's row, which the platform's package-less record is not. The pins do go red without the line, and the earlier #37013 pin in this file uses the same harness shape; but the acceptance's restart pin rides this door, not `rollbackMetaItem`, where the scenario is reachable through a bare rollback, and the note's "Before, both doors wrote the version back" holds for `revertCommit` only on such a row.
- N3 (nit) — "of a failed batch row write" in `.changeset/37013-platform-skill-own-slot.md`, see ②.
- N4 (nit) — the PR body's "Acceptance notes" still say the 37013 note "still carries ... 'never inside a publish snapshot'" and is "outside this claim's file surface", beside a "Deliberate correction" section that rewrites it; and that section says the PR made the note false, which is true of two of its three sentences. PR-body prose only.
- N5 (nit) — `refusePlatformRecordRestore` reads the mark off the row's body alone, while the protocol's own reader of the same fact, `isPlatformRecordRow` (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts:1867`), also requires an empty package column. They agree on every row the current doors write. On a package-bound row whose body keeps the mark and names no package they differ, and the refusal would then prescribe naming the package the caller already named.

Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxba3jmfHtmkWfFXfVTc` (an isolated sub-agent of this session, read-only; the dispatch order was not an input)

**VERDICT: PASS**
